items.grounds: Re-derived both ways from bytes. Parashah inventory (single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets, never a driver): MT 42:25 carries PE and MT 42:17 SAMEKH, so the mark claims are type-correct. The shipped boundary field's entire close argument is the PE sentence, and a programmatic scan of every field of the row finds no koh-amar formula anywhere (no skeleton כה אמר (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: skeleton), no 'says'); the row's only engagement with oshb:Isa.43.1 is the name-pair continuity device בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) in device_notes, read stem-level against יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, tier: byte), which argues cohesion across the close seam rather than a break. The signal that carries the seam is the divine-frame onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte); skeleton sweep of the formula: 48 verses book-wide, exactly 4 in chs 41-43 (oshb:Isa.42.5, oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.14, oshb:Isa.43.16), all divine-owned since the four royal-messenger sites are confined to chs 36-37 (36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) -- the auditor's digits hold. Tested the other way: nothing in the shipped row supplies a tier-1 close warrant that the auditor missed. Severity: the seam location is byte-sound and the PE claim is byte-true, so there is no load-bearing boundary defect and no byte-false load-bearing claim (not high); a close warranted only by a tier-3 mark that 'corroborates' an unnamed break is a defective warrant not alone load-bearing, and it is more than a disclosure slip because the seam-carrying signal is absent from the record (not low). Medium as filed.

Re-collated from tokens spliced out of the staged text: תִבְעַר (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte), the attested token inside וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte), re-collates against oshb:Isa.42.25 at SKELETON tier; וַתִּבְעַר (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte), the attested token inside וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte), re-collates against oshb:Isa.43.2 at NONE. The shipped sentence states one symmetric result, 'the attested tokens returning tier NONE', so it is byte-false in the 43:2-to-42:25 direction exactly as filed; the mechanism is the dagesh and prefixed vav of the 42:25 form, which drop only at skeleton tier. Tested the other way: the row's prose 'sharing only the fire-verb stem' is itself accurate and the device is disclosed as a cross-seam device, so the cut is not disturbed and nothing load-bearing turns on the label (not high). But under the tier-disclosure standard the named tier IS the byte-grounded claim, and on a device straddling the row's own close seam none-for-skeleton understates the cross-seam counter-pressure the cohesion rule exists to surface: a defective tier claim not alone load-bearing. Medium as filed.

The rejected-alternative sentence is as the auditor quotes it: its sole refusal ground is an absence-of-form claim keyed to web:Isa.42.21 with no pointed splice and no tier, and its only extent statement is 'through to the chapter's close'. Bytes: יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר (oshb:Isa.42.21, tier: byte) opens on the divine name as grammatical subject, its verbs carry the prefix-conjugation yod of third-person forms, and it has no vocative, no imperative and no speech frame -- skeleton sweep of the koh-amar formula places no site between oshb:Isa.42.5 and oshb:Isa.43.1 -- so the form claim is true and the rival rightly refused; the translation witness corroborates the absence, “It pleased Yahweh, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law and make it honorable.” (web:Isa.42.21), a third-person statement. Tested the other way: the finding is not overreach, because form-class labels are byte-checkable claims under the tier-disclosure standard and pointed splices are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, and this one is the strongest rival's only ground; and in a row whose close carries no tier-1 warrant the chapter-keyed extent clause is the row's sole statement of where the unit ends, tier-4 metadata standing in for an argument. True claim, rightly refused rival, wrong evidencing: defective warrant not alone load-bearing (not high, the boundary is sound; not low, it is the only ground for the strongest rival plus a tier-4 extent). Medium as filed.

Same device, opening-seam side, re-collated from spliced tokens: תִבְעַר (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.25 = SKELETON; וַתִּבְעַר (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.43.2 = NONE. The shipped sentence enumerates skeleton by name among the tiers at which the attested tokens fail, so it is byte-false as written in the 43:2-to-42:25 direction, exactly as filed. Tested the other way: the row's judgement that the pair argues continuity 'without disturbing the cut' survives at skeleton tier, and the cut rests on the tier-1 frame וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) -- one of exactly 4 koh-amar verses in chs 41-43 by skeleton sweep, 48 book-wide, all four divine-owned -- so nothing load-bearing turns on the label (not high). But an explicitly enumerated false tier on a device straddling the row's own opening seam is a defective claim under the tier-disclosure standard, not a mechanical slip (not low). Medium as filed.

Byte tie verified: עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte) re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.42.19, where it stands inside וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.42.19, tier: byte), and at NONE against oshb:Isa.43.9; a pointed-form sweep of that exact token returns exactly 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (oshb:Isa.42.19, oshb:Isa.43.8), so the backward echo is real and exclusive. The incoherence is in the record, not the seam: this row's refusal clause says the 43:8 summons reaches 'back rather than forward into the nations' gathering', while the neighbor row that opens at 43:8 grounds its onset on that same directive הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte) 'turning into' כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, tier: byte). One row denies the forward affinity the other's onset depends on. Tested the other way: the two rows are reconcilable only by rewording (a backward lexical echo carried by a verse that nonetheless opens the next unit), not as shipped; and both keep the 43:7|43:8 cut, with no parashah mark at MT 43:7 and SAMEKH only at MT 43:10 and 43:13 (single-witness, tier-3), so no span moves and nothing load-bearing fails (not high). A seam pair that characterizes the shared onset verse's affinity in opposite directions inside its load-bearing fields is a defective warrant not alone load-bearing, not a mechanical shortfall (not low). Medium as filed.

Witness re-check: the three curly runs are verbatim WEB after punctuation normalization at web:Isa.43.8 (“Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.” is the whole verse), web:Isa.43.9 (ellipsis-aware) and web:Isa.43.10, while the MT bytes the row binds them to -- הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte), כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, tier: byte), אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.10, tier: byte) -- carry no English, so each '(oshb:...)' after an English run names the wrong witness. WEB sets the 43:10 inner quotation in curly marks, “You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh (web:Isa.43.10), and the row's run replaces them with straight ASCII marks, so that run is not character-verbatim as shipped. Tested the other way: the staged quote checker returns GREEN on this row, but only because it binds each curly run to any web: ref within 200 characters with one-verse slack -- the 43:9 and 43:10 runs pass against the later web:Isa.43.10 citation and the 43:8 run is never checked at all -- so the misattribution is real and invisible to the suite, which is the auditor's point, not a refutation. Three false witness bindings in the load-bearing field plus one non-verbatim run, with no boundary claim turning on the witness label: defective citation claims not alone load-bearing (not high; not low, since a wrong witness on a quotation is a false claim, not a missing tag). Medium as filed.

The field reads exactly as quoted and ends without any refusal clause; the rival it names, folding the row into the preceding fear-not oracle, is the row's strongest and is answered nowhere in the field. The only onset ground in the row is the participant shift at הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte), which the row itself hedges for want of a morphology layer; from the bytes the shift is visible whichever way the opening verb is read (perfect or imperative), since the first-person creator speech closing on בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף עֲשִׂיתִֽיו (oshb:Isa.43.7, tier: byte) gives way to a third-party object, a blind people with eyes, and then to the nations summons כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, tier: byte) -- so a one-clause refusal was available and the auditor's proposed ground is byte-supportable, with one caveat for the docket: 43:7 itself already carries third-person suffixes on the triad, so 'second person running through 43:1-43:7' should be worded to the verse where the address is second person. One correction to the finding's ancillary claim: only the preceding neighbor carries an explicit refusal clause; the following neighbor's field likewise states its rival's case without refusing it, so 'neighbor rows on both sides' is half wrong -- immaterial to this item. No parashah mark sits at MT 43:7 (SAMEKH segs in this stretch: MT 43:10, 43:13, 43:15, single-witness), so the record's rejection of the fold rests entirely on an unstated ground: a defective warrant not alone load-bearing, the seam being carried from the other side by the closing triad and the 43:9 address change (not high; not low, since the strongest rival is left unadjudicated, not merely under-tagged). Medium as filed.
